messages:
Anika (Vendor Ops): Heads-up: Saffron AI (India) sent invoice INV-2026 for fine-tuning work. They charged 18% GST and asked us to gross-up for 10% Indian withholding (TDS) — says clause 7.4 in SOW requires net payment. They want Redwood to pay the tax on their behalf.

Jo (Finance): Do we have a gross-up clause in the SOW? If so we might be contractually bound. If not, default is payer deducts TDS where required by Indian law.

Anika (Vendor Ops): Clause 7.4 is vague. It mentions "taxes and withholdings as required by law" but also a supplier indemnity paragraph. Not an explicit gross-up.

Ravi (Tax APAC): Quick checklist: 1) Is the supplier Indian tax resident? (likely yes). 2) If Indian resident, TDS rules apply on payments for technical services, but payer deducts and remits; gross-up only if contract requires. 3) If they claim non-resident status or treaty relief, they need Indian TRC (Tax Residency Certificate), Form 10F, and a withholding tax exemption certificate from Indian tax authorities.

Hannah (Payments): From payments side: if we don't gross-up, we deduct 10% at source, remit to Indian govt and provide TDS certificate (Form 16A) to vendor. We need vendor PAN to remit correctly.

Anika (Vendor Ops): Vendor emailed saying: "We're registered Indian company (GSTIN: 29AAXCM1234M1Z5), want Redwood to gross-up as our AP team says it's Redwood policy to gross-up for foreign tech buyers. Please confirm or we'll hold the invoice." They attached an invoice PDF and a scanned PAN.

Jo (Finance): Don't let them hold payment as a negotiation tactic. We need to respond with what we need.

Ravi (Tax APAC): Draft reply below 12 please review and shorten if needed:

```
Hi Saffron AI team,

Thanks for the invoice. A few items required to process payment:
1) Confirm whether Saffron AI is an Indian tax resident (PAN attached suggests yes).
2) Provide GSTIN and confirm the GST classification on the invoice (you have 18%).
3) Provide the SOW/contract clause that you rely on for gross-up. Absent an explicit gross-up clause we are required by Indian law (section 195/194J as applicable) to deduct withholding and remit to the Indian government.
4) If you claim any treaty relief or exemption, please provide your Indian Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and Form 10F and any Indian withholding certificate permitting lower/no withholding.

If we do not receive a contractual gross-up obligation or official exemption, Redwood will deduct the applicable TDS (10%) and remit on your behalf. We will issue the TDS certificate post-remittance. If you prefer Redwood to remit a higher grossed-up amount, please provide a signed contract amendment referencing the gross-up obligation.

Please upload documents to the secure vendor portal so AP can proceed.

Best,
Ravi (Tax APAC)
```

Hannah (Payments): Add: "Please confirm the exact remittance name that matches your GST/PAN." Also mention timeline: upload within 5 business days or we will withhold.

Anika (Vendor Ops): Sent that to vendor. Vendor replied: "We are Indian resident. We cannot accept TDS deduction because it impacts our cashflow. We have a clause in SOW that says 'full payment without reduction' - see attached signed SOW pg3." They attached SOW excerpt.

Jo (Finance): If they have a signed gross-up clause, we need legal review and management sign-off. Can you attach SOW and highlight clause?

Ravi (Tax APAC): I'll review the SOW. Contractual gross-up would mean Redwood pays additional amount so vendor receives invoice amount net of tax. We'll need CFO approval. Also confirm whether the SOW references gross-up for "taxes imposed by law" vs specifically withholding — wording matters.

Anika (Vendor Ops): Uploaded SOW and invoice to shared drive, highlighted clause. Also asked vendor for their monthly TDS certificate history (they offered but didn't attach).

Ravi (Tax APAC): If we agree to gross-up, AP workflow: calculate gross-up amount using formula: gross_payment = net_amount / (1 - withholding_rate). Example: net 100 -> gross = 100 / 0.9 = 111.11, with 11.11 paid as additional to cover 10% withholding. We must also ensure VAT/GST treatment still correct on grossed-up number.

Jo (Finance): I don't love setting precedent. Let's loop in Legal and CFO. For this invoice amount (INR ~1,800,000) the gross-up delta is material. But if contract requires it, we should comply.

Hannah (Payments): Meanwhile I'll hold disbursement and flag for Legal review. If Legal ok with gross-up, tell AP to compute gross payment and route to treasury for funding in INR.

Saffron AI Pvt Ltd: Vendor: Thanks. We'll send a signed amendment if needed but prefer quick payment. Can Redwood provide a one-time netting or issue a PO amendment?

Ravi (Tax APAC): Reply to vendor: we can expedite if you sign contract amendment accepting Redwood's calculation and provide PAN/GST/TDS history. Otherwise Redwood will deduct TDS and remit.

Anika (Vendor Ops): Sent message. Legal pinged me, wants to review clause and vendor's proposed amendment. I'll schedule a quick call with vendor and Legal. Closing notes: request vendor docs up front during onboarding to avoid this next time. :spiral_calendar:
